hook.line: Vale lent Tomás money for flour, and she wants it back. She does not shout: she starts a sentence and lets the silence finish it.
hook.es: Como no me devuelvas la plata esta semana, se acabó.
hook.en: If you don't pay me back this week, that's it.

examples.es: Como no me devolviste la plata, no te presto más.
examples.en: Since you didn't pay me back, I'm not lending you any more.

rule: A threat often starts with *como* and the 'not yet, but if' verb form: *Como me entere...*, *Como llegues tarde...* It means *if*, only sharper: if that happens, watch out. What follows may be vague, or missing; the silence is the threat (*ya verás*). Compare *como* with a plain verb, which only gives a reason: *Como no me devolviste la plata*, since you didn't. Spot the difference by the verb: *entere*, *devuelvas*, *llegues* look ahead.
smallPrint: Teachers call this conditional *como* with the subjunctive. It always takes the subjunctive; with the indicative, *como* means since.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *llegues* or *llegaste*: Como ___ tarde otra vez, ya verás. (a warning). Type the whole sentence.
yourTurn.answer: Como llegues tarde otra vez, ya verás.
yourTurn.why: A threat looks ahead, so the 'if it happens' form *llegues*.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *devuelvas* or *devolviste*: Como no me ___ la plata esta semana, se acabó. (a warning to a friend). Type the whole sentence.
yourTurn.answer: Como no me devuelvas la plata esta semana, se acabó.

yourTurn.prompt: If I find out you didn't go to class, you're grounded. (to a friend)
yourTurn.answer: Como me entere de que no fuiste a clase, te quedas sin salir.
yourTurn.why: *Como me entere* is the threat, and the result follows after the comma.

yourTurn.prompt: If she has forgotten the keys, we can't get in.
yourTurn.answer: Como se haya olvidado de las llaves, no entramos.
accept: Como se le hayan olvidado las llaves, no entramos.
yourTurn.why: *Se haya olvidado* is the looking ahead form of has forgotten.

yourTurn.prompt: Since you didn't pay me back, I'm not lending you any more. (a reason, not a threat; to a friend)
yourTurn.answer: Como no me devolviste la plata, no te presto más.
yourTurn.why: A real past fact, so the plain past verb and *como* means since.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it a warning to two friends (you all): *Como llegues tarde otra vez, ya verás.*
yourTurn.answer: Como lleguen tarde otra vez, ya verán.
yourTurn.why: Both the threat verb and *verán* move to the *ustedes* form.

yourTurn.prompt: If you don't call me tonight, that's it. (to a friend)
yourTurn.answer: Como no me llames esta noche, se acabó.
yourTurn.why: Same frame: *como no* plus the looking ahead form, *llames*.

pitfalls.wrong: Como me enteré de que mentiste, se acabó.
pitfalls.right: Como me entere de que mentiste, se acabó.
pitfalls.why: Almost. *Enteré* says it already happened, so it only means since; the threat needs *entere*.

pitfalls.wrong: Como no me devuelves la plata, se acabó.
pitfalls.right: Como no me devuelvas la plata, se acabó.
pitfalls.why: A threat points ahead, so *devuelvas* rather than *devuelves*.

pitfalls.wrong: Si llegues tarde otra vez, ya verás.
pitfalls.right: Como llegues tarde otra vez, ya verás.
pitfalls.why: With *si* it would be *si llegas*. The sharper threat is *como* plus *llegues*.

personal: Think of a small rule where you live. Write a threat with *Como...* and a looking ahead verb, then stop at the comma or add *ya verás*.
